claim: Minimization and maximization gaps admit pointwise and infimum/supremum ceilings, with strict/weak threshold distinction.
assumptions: Feasible incumbent, objective uniformly bounded on the nonempty domain for the infimum/supremum assertion.
falsifier: Empty or unbounded domain; equality at target allowed.
independent_check: Inspected minInterval/maxInterval and derived lower/upper gap by subtracting common feasible incumbent; checked equality control U=10,L=9,J=9.
remaining_obligation: Uniform bound and nonempty feasible set must be supplied in every application.
v0_6_admissible_wording: For a feasible incumbent and valid objective floor or ceiling, the optimality gap is bounded by the difference from that floor or ceiling. Strict exclusion of an inclusive target requires a strict bound unless nonattainment is proved.

claim: Nonattainment of the floor permits strict exclusion even where the ceiling equals the target.
assumptions: A separate proof excludes attainment by every admissible candidate.
falsifier: A feasible candidate at the floor invalidates the additional premise.
independent_check: Derived J(x)>L for every feasible x when L is not attained; therefore U-J(x)<U-L. Counterexample at attainment checked.
remaining_obligation: Nonattainment must be established, not inferred from solver tolerance.
v0_6_admissible_wording: At a ceiling equal to the target, strict exclusion is valid only if no admissible candidate attains the relevant floor (or an equivalent strict bound is proved).

claim: Finite weighted opportunity bounds admit missing-case fallback floors at original weights.
assumptions: Nonnegative weights, all cases covered, common objective and admissible candidate. Total weight one for mean units.
falsifier: Missing mass, wrong denominator or negative weight.
independent_check: Summed individual inequalities with nonnegative weights; tested missing mass (0,4) at equal weights and negative-weight reversal. A retains two invalid paths.
remaining_obligation: A missing baseline is not repaired by a fallback lower bound; need a valid baseline value and bound per weighted case; otherwise report incomplete coverage or separately justified enclosing baseline.
v0_6_admissible_wording: Finite weighted opportunity ceilings preserve original nonnegative weights. For a missing floor a valid fallback floor may be substituted without dropping weight, provided a valid baseline is available. Ineligible baselines remain explicitly unresolved; no full-panel mean certificate follows by omission.

claim: Relaxed/physical/observation-compatible/deadline-constrained infima are ordered; finer observations can be ignored.
assumptions: Common horizon, cost, nonempty nested sets, bounded values, baseline allowed.
falsifier: A deadline or information mismatch invalidates nesting.
independent_check: Inspected operationalChain and ignoreInformation, proved infimum order for inclusion and refinement of observation partitions. Reconstructed issued E decisions; actual future branch revealed only in planning approximation.
remaining_obligation: Physical, adapted and deadline-feasible sets must truly nest under same objective; more information may incur compute or acquisition cost.
v0_6_admissible_wording: With a common objective and nested feasible domains, the relaxed, physical, observation-compatible and deadline-constrained infima are ordered. A policy can ignore extra observations only when refinement and the feasible-policy contract permit it.

claim: A cost floor excludes positive net value if gross ceiling is no greater; discounts preserve pointwise bounds.
assumptions: Correct unit/horizon tags, justified floor, nonnegative weights, proper pathwise accounting.
falsifier: Mislabelled inputs, mixing dollars and energy or cross-horizon costs.
independent_check: Subtracted implementation floor and multiplied by nonnegative discount weights; tested kWh/MWh scale error. Lean Amount tags encode same type, not real unit calibration.
remaining_obligation: No justified implementation-cost floor or field net cash flows in W06; unit and horizon semantics require independent bridge.
v0_6_admissible_wording: A valid gross opportunity ceiling no greater than a justified implementation-cost floor excludes positive modeled net benefit. Nonnegative discounts preserve the bound if cash flows, units and horizons match.

claim: Boxed and mixed-row LP multipliers give exact lower certificates for feasible points.
assumptions: True row/variable activity intervals, exact signed multipliers and matrix products for the same representation.
falsifier: Positive multiplier on upper-only row; unsupported one-sided residual sign.
independent_check: Independently rebuilt LP floors in A, rational UC and AC, including exact signed row-endpoint and box residual sums; wrong-sign control reproduced.
remaining_obligation: One-sided rows need admissible multipliers; boxes must include original feasible set.
v0_6_admissible_wording: For a finite valid box and correctly signed row multipliers, the exact residual-and-endpoint expression is a lower bound; solver-reported dual feasibility is not necessary for this boxed certificate.

claim: Upper feasible gain and bounded transfer/enclosure require admissible candidates and explicit model maps or allowances.
assumptions: Actual model-domain membership and one-sided objective domination.
falsifier: A primal residual alone cannot prove feasibility.
independent_check: Derived transfer by composing feasible model map and one-sided objective inequality; verified AC rank-one lift and UC exact primal; checked infeasible incumbent/rounding counterexamples.
remaining_obligation: Map, cost allowance, and actual feasibility must be demonstrated in each model.
v0_6_admissible_wording: A feasible improving candidate provides a lower bound on recoverable gain; transfer and enclosure require verified feasibility and explicit one-sided cost domination or allowance.

claim: Conditional cost comparison preserves the imposed service, risk and stock contract. Uniform per-scenario loss bounds transfer to any monotone cash-shifting risk measure.
assumptions: All applicable dimensions constrained and pointwise losses bounded; risk assumptions verified for the selected functional.
falsifier: Mean gain alone fails a two-point CVaR counterexample.
independent_check: Derived pointwise J0(s)≤J(s)+e then monotonicity and cash translation; verified mean falls 50→40 while upper-half tail rises 50→80 in source control.
remaining_obligation: Lean contractCost represents service/risk/stock by scalar functions; complete hourly service, multivariate risk, activation requirements and risk-functional premises must be verified separately.
v0_6_admissible_wording: A cost ceiling applies within the imposed service, risk and stock contract. A uniform per-scenario loss bound transfers to a monotone cash-translating risk functional with the required shift property; an average gain alone does not imply tail-risk improvement.

claim: Nonpositive expected penalties for every common policy turn augmented path floors into an aggregate lower bound.
assumptions: Nonnegative weights and a policy-wide centering inequality with respect to the same information/measure.
falsifier: A positive expected penalty can fabricate a false floor.
independent_check: Summed augmented floors and used nonpositive expected penalty for every admissible common policy; positive penalty=1 at true J=0 counterexample.
remaining_obligation: No calibrated policy-wide martingale/centering certificate for operational E; do not infer it from one policy.
v0_6_admissible_wording: Information-relaxed path floors yield an operational aggregate floor only when penalty centering or a nonpositive expectation is proved for every admissible policy under the same weights and information pattern.

claim: A two-state common-action problem has perfect-foresight gap 1/2 and centered bound gap zero.
assumptions: Illustrative model with one shared action and two equiprobable indistinguishable states.
falsifier: Scenario-specific admissible actions would change the operational contract.
independent_check: Enumerated two shared actions with equal state weights; common optimum 1/2, PF optimum 0; centered bounds recover 1/2. Reran finite controls.
remaining_obligation: Illustrative model only, not evidence for E policy gap.
v0_6_admissible_wording: The two-state toy problem exhibits a 1/2 perfect-foresight gap; a centered penalty closes that bound gap exactly under its shared-action contract.

claim: A continuous constant inventory credit telescopes and a uniform feasible closing repair of cost K caps the difference of the terminal-contract infima.
assumptions: Identical opening positions for the accounting comparison, uniform cross-contract repair for the full operational premium.
falsifier: A narrow SOC box alone supplies no bound in dollars.
independent_check: Telescoping cancellation by summation; derived infimum premium by uniform repair with cost ≤K; arbitrary replacement price disproves capacity-only dollar bound.
remaining_obligation: Uniform closing repair not established for actual reserve/control applications; fixed credit alone is not total-cost premium.
v0_6_admissible_wording: Constant inventory marks telescope along a continuous path. A uniform feasible cross-contract repair costing at most K bounds the terminal-contract premium; capacity and inventory mark alone do not bound replacement costs generally.
